verification_report.summary:
All statements and proofs in the submitted TeX pass sequential verification under the four explicitly stipulated internal premises. No critical errors or gaps were found.

For the envelope lemma, the obstacle bounds establish a genuine envelope of ordinary minimal type, and quasi-continuity permits the stated contact theorem. The inverse tau exists, is convex, and has derivative in (0,1]. A common quadratic correction and decreasing radial convolutions give lower curvature bounds -theta-epsilon_j beta without using a local potential for theta. The chain map is nondecreasing in both inputs, so decreasing convex approximations also give decreasing transformed potentials. Uniform local mixed-mass bounds remove the curvature-error terms; capacity convergence of the derivative factors and uniform capacity control justify the weighted-product limit. Canonical analytic extension, ordered contact, the reciprocal derivative identity and contact support then prove the claimed inequality.

For the proposition, zero domination upgrades the MA-essential depth T to x=V-u<=T outside a pluripolar set, so the bound also holds for nu. The cutoff weights have the required C^{1,1} regularity. Tonelli gives K=3max(1,M), and Chebyshev yields the stated growth exponent beta=1+1/(2N). The identity (n+1/2)/N=1/2 gives the Cauchy--Schwarz energy bound. Normalizing p_s itself and using its mass lower bound yields -sup p_s<=KB/ell^2. Finite A_theta(nu) therefore gives integral W_s(x)dnu<=A+KB/ell^2. The tail argument remains valid near T, including possible mass at x=T. Layer cake correctly includes r, with r/(beta-r)=4N+1.

All constants are uniform in u and s. Explicitly, with D=3max(1,M)/ell^2, one permissible final constant is max(2^r, 1+(4N+1)2^(1+2/N)max(1,D)), depending only on n,ell,M. Uniform integrability follows from the uniform L^r bound for V-u and the fixed integrable summand -V; no L^r bound for V is asserted.

The cited Proposition 5.1 and Lemma 5.1 were confirmed in the supplied archive and through the required theorem-search-first, web-fallback workflow. Their role is attribution; the submitted arguments independently establish the claims with the stated finite-A hypothesis. The source's stronger measure-domination assumption and its other global assumptions are not imported. See [XL26, Section 5.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13446v1).
